maria_support: Heads-up — we've got a customer on hosted inference (acct: acme-prod) seeing 504s on spikes since 09:12 UTC. Support ticket linked, they report ~30% of requests hitting gateway timeouts under a ~3x burst. Logs show scale events but requests still queue.

sam_runtime: Can you paste the proxy/gateway logs and any pod events? sounds like scale up didn't finish before requests landed.

maria_support: Pastes below. Note the HPA/KEDA events look normal but pods stay in Init for ~45s.

maria_support: ```
gateway: upstream request timed out after 60.002s for req_id=... status=504
controller: KEDA scaled deployment/runner 0->3 at 09:12:14
events: pod/runner-abcde Init:ModelInit took 47.3s, readiness probe failed 3/3
container logs: [model-init] loading weights v2.1 -> took 41s, mmap fallback, warming KV cache
```

anna_ops: Hmm model-init + readinessProbe is the suspect. What's readinessProbe config? If it's too agressive pods get marked unready and killed while model still loads.

maria_support: readinessProbe configured: exec curl localhost:8080/health || exit 1, initialDelaySeconds=5, periodSeconds=5, failureThreshold=3.

jonalytics: That's the issue — initialDelay 5s + model load ~40s -> kube kills after ~20s. KEDA scales but pods never become ready. Gateway sends traffic and times out.

sam_runtime: Agree. Also seeing KEDA scaler default pollInterval 30s and cooldown 300s in this cluster. That makes reaction choppy for short bursts. Two layers of mismatch: probe too-tight + scaler polling too-sparse.

maria_support: Customer says this started after the new model variant rolled last week (weights larger). Are we running any lazy load or mmap that increased load time?

sam_runtime: Yes the new variant has larger checkpoint and falls back to mmap causing longer cold-init. Runtime team rollout changed quantization and memmap fallback last Tuesday.

dev-bot: Deploy event: rollout/runner-model-v2 at 2026-03-12T07:33:12Z (image: rwinf/runner:v2.1).

anna_ops: Short-term mitigation options: 1) bump readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to 60+ for that deployment, 2) increase failureThreshold/periodSeconds, or 3) enable small pre-warmed pool (dedicated ephemeral) for that customer.

maria_support: I've suggested initialDelay=70 and failureThreshold=3 to the customer. They asked for a recommended config and repro steps. Can we provide a safe quick patch?

sam_runtime: For a quick patch set initialDelaySeconds=80 and periodSeconds=10. Also add a postStart hook to touch /ready-file after model init completes. Example: 

sam_runtime: ```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /live
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
  periodSeconds: 10
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 80
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
lifecycle:
  postStart:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/app/bin/warmup && touch /tmp/ready"]
```

jonalytics: Also suggest updating KEDA ScaledObject to pollInterval: 5 and cooldownPeriod: 30 for this workload class so scaler notices short bursts faster (work with infra). But be careful, lower pollInterval increases API calls.

anna_ops: We should add a gating config in the ModelOnboard doc: when checkpoint size > X, set probe.delay >= Y and add mmap-awareness. Prevent future rollouts from using default probe.

maria_support: Repro steps I documented for support: 
1) Simulate burst with boomload script sending 200 rps for 15s targeting a cold pool.
2) Observe KEDA scale event in controller logs.
3) Check pod events -> readiness failures and model-init duration in container logs.
4) See gateway 504 for requests that arrived before ready.

maria_support: Boomscript example: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do siege -c200 -t15S https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done
```

sam_runtime: Good. For permanent fix options: 1) pre-warm pool (dedicated), 2) reduce model cold-start via smaller quantized variant, 3) async model loading with early health endpoint that only flips ready after KV warmup.

anna_ops: Also check HPA metrics — if HPA uses CPU and model init doesn't spike CPU until after weights mapped, you get delayed HPA reaction. Prefer queue-length or custom metrics for this service (keda scaledobject queueLength/redis).

maria_support: Customer asked if this could be a billing/auth thing because tokens succeeded then 504s. I confirmed auth calls succeeded (200) and token billing checks were normal. So it's infrastructure coldstart.

sam_runtime: I'll open a runtime task to add a model-init readiness gate and update the onboarding checklist. Also will propose a short-term infra change to allow lower KEDA pollInterval for high-priority tenants.

dev-bot: Incident created: rwinf-incident-2239998888 (priority: P2) assigned to sam_runtime.

maria_support: Assigning to support + infra for customer follow-up. I'm sending the suggested probe patch now, and recommending a temporary dedicated warm pool until we push the runtime fix.

jonalytics: If anyone needs a quick log grep: kubectl describe deploy/runner -n prod | grep -A5 Events

anna_ops: Let's also add an alert on >5% 504s over 1m for hosted inference routes tied to scale events — that will catch regressions.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll update the ticket with repro steps, config snippet, and timeframe. Will circle back when infra confirms KEDA tweak. :thumbsup:

sam_runtime: thx — I'll post follow-up patch link once done.
